requirements.text: The MultiMahjongServer shall reside on a central computer connected to a TCP/IP network with a unique IP address.
The MultiMahjongServer shall allow connections from MultiMahjongClients and communicate using IP.
The MultiMahjongServer shall relay data between connected MultiMahjongClients.
The MultiMahjongClient shall support both single-player (against 3 computer opponents) and multi-player (up to 4 players) modes.
The MultiMahjongClient shall allow users to create new games, join existing games, or quit the program.
The MultiMahjongClient shall enforce Chinese Mahjong rules for all moves.
The MultiMahjongClient shall provide a graphical user interface for game interaction using mouse and keyboard.
The MultiMahjongClient shall display the current user's tiles, the wall, other players' tile backs, revealed/exposed sets, and the last discard.
The MultiMahjongClient shall provide buttons for game actions (pick up, discard, Chow, Pung, Kong, Mahjong) that are enabled only when the action is valid.
Computer Opponents shall play according to Chinese Mahjong rules and be unable to see concealed tiles of other players.
Computer Opponents must respond to game actions within 1 minute.
The MultiMahjongServer must support up to 10 simultaneous games (40 players).
The MultiMahjongClient must calculate valid Chow/Pung/Kong/Mahjong moves within 5 seconds of a discard.
No encryption is required for data exchange as no private information is transmitted.
The system shall be implemented using JDK 1.2 and follow Sun Microsystems coding conventions.
The software shall run on Windows 95/98/NT, Macintosh OS 8, and Solaris 2.6/7.
The GUI shall be designed for a screen resolution of 800x600 pixels with 16-bit color.
The system shall display a dialogue box for all fatal and non-fatal errors, with the ability to terminate on fatal errors.
The product shall include an administrator's manual for the server and a user's manual for the client in electronic format.
